chapter: Blackbirds, Carmen Jones and the Ziegfeld Follies
title: The show Carmen Jones: prize fighter, country club scene and treadmill race
summary: He recalls a 25-person all-colored show with prize fighter Erskine Miller, the Chicago Southside Country Club number, a prize fight arena and a treadmill racetrack.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Can you tell me a little bit about that show, "Carmen Jones?"

"Carmen Jones" had Erskine Miller who was a prize fighter and he had -- I can't remember all the people that were in that show. It had a cast of about 25 people and Buck and I was Rum and Dink and the managers of Erskine Miller. I was the manager and Buck was my assistant, you know. So we had four or five good singing in the show and we did what you call a duet, five-part harmony. "Chicago" was one of the main songs. "Chicago, Chicago, off to Chicago Whizzing away on the track Clickety-Clack, Clickety-Clack Clickety-Clack" -- I can't think of that song. However, we'd sing the song and did a number in the show called "Chicago Southside Country Club," that

was the scene, it was an outstanding scene where everybody was dressed in the same color, blue, two or three tones of different blues. It was a beautiful thing and we did a card scene number and this country club number. That was about the biggest thing they had in the show. Then they had the prize fight arena which was good.
Yeah. We did the prize fight, you know. That was good, too.
This was all part of the show, all contained in the show.

And in that other play they had a racetrack treadmill right on the stage where the horses ran on the stage on a mill. You'd see one horse passing the other horse. I didn't get to that part, couldn't think of it. And we'd do 'Carmen Jones' in 1931 --
